sentences.text: Platytholus was a small, bipedal dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Hell Creek Formation in the United States.
This genus contains only one known species, P. clemensi, recognized from a partial skull featuring a distinct low, broad, and rectangular dome shape.

Its skull incorporated supraorbital and postorbital bones into the dome structure, unlike some relatives where these bones form distinct lobes, and the sides display unique, sharp-tipped, roof-tile-like ornamentation found nowhere else.
The sides of Platytholus's skull feature unique, sharp-tipped, roof-tile-like ornamentation found nowhere else.
The extensive fusion and developed dome state suggest the holotype specimen represents an adult animal.
The holotype specimen (MOR 2915) was discovered by Jack Horner in the early 2000s in Garfield County, Montana, within the latest Maastrichtian sediments of the Hell Creek Formation.

Platytholus clemensi was formally described as a new genus and species in 2023 by Horner, Goodwin, and Evans, with the genus name combining Greek roots meaning "flattened" or "wide" and "small domed hill," while the species name honors the American paleontologist William A. Clemens Jr.
Phylogenetic analysis places Platytholus as a derived member of the Pachycephalosaurinae clade.
Platytholus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
It lived alongside the smaller Sphaerotholus and the larger Pachycephalosaurus.
The exact phylogenetic position of Platytholus is debated and considered weakly supported due to poor preservation of the squamosal ornamentation.
